name: Madrid Transit Pack
author: xoaninc
description:
Standardized Madrid train types, one per real network: Metro narrow-profile (CAF S/3000, lines 1-5 and the Ramal), Metro wide-profile (S/8000-9000, lines 6-12), Metro Ligero (Citadis 302) and Cercanías Madrid (S/452 Alstom X'Trapolis). Real-world specs from official technical documentation and as-built project records: curve radii down to 90 m on the historic narrow-profile lines and 250 m on the wide-profile network, gradients set to what the network actually climbs (5.2% narrow-profile, 4% wide-profile), real platform lengths (60-115 m), cheaper narrow-profile tunnels, and 140 km/h high-capacity commuter EMUs with 100/200 m consists. Maintenance at parity with vanilla types. One type per network means branches and shared tracks between lines of the same network are fully compatible.

**Subway Builder 1.7:** all four types declare the new cant fields (`maxCantMm` / `maxCantDeficiencyMm`), so curve speed on newly built track follows the 1.7 model instead of falling back to the engine's generic 150 mm. Metro Ligero now takes the new vanilla `light-rail` as its reference instead of `tram`: maintenance at light-rail parity, the new grade-crossing speed limit (15.65 m/s over a 150 m approach), and no mixed-traffic street running — ML1-ML3 run on their own reserved right of way, so the flag inherited from the tram is gone. Reversing dwell (`turnaroundTimeSeconds`) declared on every type.

**Line migration:** a main-menu tool that truly moves existing lines onto the pack's types — the game's converter only relabels. It retypes track and full track groups, extends platforms to the type's maximum by redistributing existing alignment (never inventing geometry), regenerates crossovers with the game's exact geometry (widening their window when the target radius needs it), conforms curves and gradients to the type's standard, deletes the line's trains and leaves it stopped, and writes a new save — chaining several lines into a single file. Lines sharing track migrate together or not at all; anything unsolvable is listed and gated behind an explicit checkbox. It refuses saves with an open track-edit session, whose snapshot would restore un-migrated track over a converted line, and flags saved blueprints that reference the migrated type. The in-game panel previews physical train fit, radii and gradients per line and target, in English and Spanish.

Cercanías stats derived from DanielD1909's danTrains (MIT), verified against the real S/452 specs. Full sources and documentation in the README
